human_actions_pending.context: The live site still has neither the on-leave wipe nor the /explain-that-inchi/__leave endpoint. The image builds clean and was smoke-tested locally (COOP/COEP on every route, 204 + Clear-Site-Data on __leave, gzip_static serving 51 KB for the main asset with immutable cache headers). Carried over from the previous session and still the top item.

human_actions_pending.action: Curl __leave through the upstream proxy after deploying
human_actions_pending.context: The proxy's HTTP Basic gate may 401 the beacon. A 401 carries no Clear-Site-Data header, so the cache purge silently does nothing and privacy 3(4) becomes false in production. This is the only link in the chain never tested outside a local container. Command: curl -sI -u eti -X POST https://cheminfo.beilstein.org/explain-that-inchi/__leave | grep -iE '^(HTTP|clear-site-data)'

human_actions_pending.action: Take the GitHub Pages site down
human_actions_pending.context: Deleting .github/workflows/deploy.yml only stopped future publishes. The gh-pages branch still exists on origin and GitHub still serves it, so a stale copy of the app is live with no __leave endpoint. Disable Pages in Settings -> Pages, then: git push origin --delete gh-pages. Left undone deliberately — outward-facing and hard to reverse.

human_actions_pending.action: Decide the Clear-Site-Data origin blast radius
human_actions_pending.context: Clear-Site-Data is scoped to the ORIGIN, not to /explain-that-inchi/. Every leave clears cache AND storage for all of cheminfo.beilstein.org. Safe only if no other application on that host stores browser state. No path-scoped variant exists; the fixes are a dedicated subdomain or dropping the purge. Warning is written into nginx.conf and leaveWipe.ts but no behaviour was changed.

human_actions_pending.action: Confirm log rotation is <= 14 days on the host
human_actions_pending.context: Privacy 2(2) promises log deletion within 2 weeks. nginx.conf defines no access_log directive, so retention is a logrotate concern on the server. Unbacked claim, carried from the previous session.

decisions.decision: The cache purge is unconditional; no opt-in toggle
decisions.rationale: Shipped first as a footer checkbox, then removed at the user's instruction. A setting that defaults to keeping the data is one almost nobody changes, and the privacy policy would then describe the minority case. Accepted cost: every reload re-downloads the whole bundle.

decisions.decision: Deleted the GitHub Pages workflow rather than fixing the code for both targets
decisions.rationale: Pages was a second live deployment nginx.conf did not govern. It had no __leave endpoint (purge silently no-op) and, because cross-origin isolation came from coi-serviceworker there, window.crossOriginIsolated was true BECAUSE the worker was registered — so the unregister guard would have torn down the very worker providing isolation on every visit. One target removes both bugs without a code change.

decisions.decision: Kept public/coi-serviceworker.js as an inert fallback
decisions.rationale: nginx sets COOP/COEP at the origin so it returns early and never registers. Harmless, and it is the safety net if the app is ever served from a host that cannot set headers.

The inherited '29 MB' was never measured and went into a legal document. Built output is 49.2 MB uncompressed, 18.4 MB of it deliberately-uncompressed WASM, and the over-the-wire figure depends on the gzip_static siblings in the image. Text now says 'several tens of megabytes'.

They are research and decision archives; gutting a record to fix a plumbing problem is the wrong trade. Consequence: the CLAUDE.md trim is NOT durable — GSD regenerates the Project and Technology Stack sections from these sources, so a future /gsd-docs-update will restore them.

decisions.decision: Did not write 51 skillOverrides for unused gsd-* skills
decisions.rationale: GSD ships /gsd-surface as its own cluster manager; individual overrides would drift against it. ~1226 est. tokens/session still available by running that command.

next_action: Rebuild and redeploy the container (docker compose up --build), then curl __leave through the proxy to confirm the 401 gate is not swallowing the Clear-Site-Data header.
context_notes: Started as 'how do I measure what is left on the client after leaving', became a measurement exercise and then a feature. Everything claimed here was measured against a real browser profile and a real nginx container, not reasoned from config — three conclusions were wrong on first pass and only caught that way (see the anti-pattern table in .continue-here.md). Repo is clean, both remotes at df4121d, 539 tests green, tsc clean. One open technical question survives: Clear-Site-Data 'cache' evicted the HTTP cache but the compiled-JS Code Cache still referenced the origin afterwards, byte-identical to the never-left baseline — program code rather than user data, but the claim 'nothing remains' would be an overclaim and the policy text is worded accordingly.
